value: Most aircraft need an annual (12 calendar months); a 100-hour applies only when carrying persons for hire or giving paid instruction in a provided aircraft.
reason: § 91.409(c)(1) exempts aircraft with a special flight permit or an experimental, light-sport or provisional certificate, so not every aircraft needs an annual.

value: The annual is time-based and applies to most aircraft, though § 91.409(c) exempts some, such as experimental ones; the 100-hour is use-based, because flying people for hire adds wear and risk.
reason: Explanation follows the corrected back and names the exemption.

value: Three takeoffs and three landings within 90 days, as sole manipulator, in the same category and class, and type if a type rating is required.
reason: § 61.57(a)(1)(ii) makes the type condition apply only "if a class or type rating is required".

value: Because the occlusion joins a cold front to a warm front, the handbook says it often brings a mixture of the weather found in both.
reason: PHAK p. 12-21 speaks of "a mixture of weather found in both warm and cold fronts", not of both kinds of weather arriving in turn.

value: At or below what ceiling, and at or below what visibility, must ATC facilities solicit PIREPs?
reason: The old front said "Below what ceiling", but AIM 7-1-18 says "at or below" for both values.
